drafted_from: tool:register-trillion-in-my-ai-apps row in tool-rows.json, read-data/mcp-registration.json, do-work/register-in-ai-apps.mjs and test/mcp-registration.test.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "Preview adding Trillion to my Cursor MCP settings, show me exactly what would change, and register it once I approve." It runs the preview first, shows the before and after lines, then registers with the review hash you approved.
no_lists_because: It names no list: it reads and edits the MCP config file of each AI app you name on your own computer.
instructions: 1. Name the AI apps by id (claude-code, codex, gemini-cli, cursor); an app not on this computer answers not_installed and nothing is created for it.

2. Say "Preview adding Trillion to <apps>"; your AI reads the row with tools:list and runs `node tools/register-trillion-in-my-ai-apps/do-work/register-in-ai-apps.mjs --action mcp-preview --client cursor` from the Workshop checkout (after npm install once); nothing is written.

3. Read each result's now (absent, registered, outdated, custom, blocked or not_installed) and its exact before and after lines; approve, then run --action mcp-register --client <ids> --reviewed <review_hash>; if a file changed since the preview every write is refused.

4. Registering keeps every other key in the file, backs the file up beside it, and reads it back; an entry named trillion that is yours (custom) is never changed or removed. Each result names the sign-in still to do in that app; use --action mcp-unregister to take the entry out again.

worked_examples.title: Preview, register and take out Trillion in Cursor
worked_examples.ask: Add Trillion to my Cursor MCP settings, showing me what changes first.
worked_examples.given: From tools/register-trillion-in-my-ai-apps/test/mcp-registration.test.mjs (the last test runs the command on a pretend home that holds only a .cursor folder): the commands are `node tools/register-trillion-in-my-ai-apps/do-work/register-in-ai-apps.mjs --action mcp-preview --client cursor`, then --action mcp-register --client cursor --reviewed <the review_hash from the preview>, then --action mcp-unregister --client cursor. Read from the same test: Cursor's file is .cursor/mcp.json and its entry is {url: "https://app.gettrillion.ai/mcp"}.
worked_examples.hands_back: The preview answers {schema, action: "mcp-preview", review_hash, results: [{client: "cursor", now: "absent", ...the file's before/after lines}]} and writes nothing. The register answers results[0].result "registered" with the backup path and the sign-in still to do, and .cursor/mcp.json then holds {"mcpServers": {"trillion": {"url": "https://app.gettrillion.ai/mcp"}}}, any other server in the file kept. Running register again answers already_registered; unregister answers removed and then already_absent. If the file holds a trillion entry pointing somewhere else (a proxy of yours) the result is custom and the file is left as it is.
